title: A line ending in \ is a line break: "Tag the release.\", then "Push the tag."
head: 03fdcd35b3478a2f1ff92dbc9c117d4cade7da81

clause.text: A paragraph's lines are joined with a space, but a `\` or two spaces at the end of a line is a **line break**, as on GitHub (CommonMark's hard line breaks): "Tag the release.\", then "Push the tag." are two lines, no backslash

scenes.caption: code-style's SKILL.md says "Tag the release.\", then "Push the tag.": two lines, no backslash
Two spaces at the end of "Tag the release." break the line too; with no \ nor spaces, it is one line

clause.text: at the end of a paragraph or a heading, escaped (`\\`), or in code, the `\` is text

scenes.caption: A \ at the end of the paragraph, escaped as \\, or in code is text: "Done.\", "a\ b", `x\ y`
